title: Marketplace release-notes sync + rollback playbook for cross-cloud launches
creator: Lina Park
description:
Goal: produce a repeatable, low-friction process to coordinate and publish release notes and marketplace listing updates across AWS, Azure, and GCP, plus a tested rollback/playbook in case a listing or SKU change causes regressions. This ticket covers orchestration (who does what, when), canonical release-notes content, automation hooks, legal/i18n signoffs, and post-launch telemetry checks.

Scope:
- Author canonical Release Notes markdown + marketplace-adapted copy (short/long descriptions, feature bullets, screenshots).
- Define and implement an automated sync flow that transforms canonical release notes into the three marketplace formats and surfaces validation errors to owners.
- Create a rollback playbook documenting steps to revert listing fields, disable new SKUs, and re-route traffic.
- Pre-launch check windows and gating: legal trademark check, pricing verification, console/API version pin.
- Post-launch monitoring runbook and dashboard checklist (availability, 4xx/5xx, onboarding success metrics).

Deliverables:
- release-notes canonical markdown template (with templating tokens for SKUs, metrics, feature flags).
- scripts/repo: tools/marketplace-sync in GitHub that outputs marketplace payloads and a validation report. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/8421)
- pre-flight checklist and signoff matrix (legal, billing, eng, docs, growth).
- rollback playbook doc with example CLI commands and Console steps.
- post-launch telemetry dashboard in Console (route: Console > Marketplace > Launches).

Timeline & milestones: 
- 2025-02-18: Canonical template draft (done).
- 2025-02-21: Engineering spike for transformation script (ENG-4732) — blocked by API schema question (resolved 02-22).
- 2025-02-24: Legal review for copy and trademark checks (owner: Jenna Ortiz).
- 2025-03-03: Dry-run publish to staging marketplaces and run monitoring checks.
- 2025-03-10: Final signoffs and production push window.

Stakeholders & contacts:
- PM: Aisha Khan (owner)
- Eng: Marco Ruiz (runtime/SDK changes), Priya Desai (backend/listing API)
- Design: Kofi Mensah (screenshots/assets, Azure screenshot variant)
- Legal: Jenna Ortiz (copy signoff)
- Growth/Partnerships: Maya Chen (marketplace account liaisons)
- Support: Ravi Patel (post-launch escalations)

Validation rules & known marketplace constraints:
- AWS Marketplace: 48–72 hour review for paid listing updates; requires unique SKU mapping and screenshot sizes 1200x627.
- Azure Marketplace: separate offer/publisher agreement; price tiers must match SKU config submitted in portal. Update propagation may be 24–48 hours.
- GCP Marketplace: uses container-based or SaaS manifests; ensure billing SKU IDs match our billing backend.

Rollback playbook summary:
- 1) Identify failing artifact (listing copy, SKU, screenshot).
- 2) If a SKU mismatch: disable incoming traffic on the Marketplace enforcer and revert to previous SKU mapping in billing service (ENG runbook ID: RB-01).
- 3) If copy causes compliance flag: revert listing via marketplace console and open escalation case with partner team (Maya).
- 4) Publish an internal incident note and update support templates with talking points.

Metrics to validate success (post-publish day-0 and day-7):
- Marketplace page availability (0% errors)
- Traffic-to-signup conversion delta <= 10% relative to baseline
- Billing/entitlement success rate >= 99.5%
- Post-launch support tickets for listing issues <= 5 first-week

Links / artifacts: 
- Canonical release notes template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/marketplace/release-notes-template
- GitHub PR (automation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8421
- Staging publish playbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/marketplace/staging-publish-runbook.pdf

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Should release notes generation be pushed to a scheduled CI job or triggered manually per launch? (Recommendation: manual trigger for first 3 launches, then schedule after confidence.)
- Who owns the final validation of region-specific screenshots? (Design to own, with PM QA.)
- Do we require a separate legal run for EU localized copy? (Legal recommend a lightweight review only for high-risk terminology.)
